title: Alexandrie: Your New Self-Hosted Knowledge Hub with Superpowers!
article: Hey fellow developers! Ever feel like your team's knowledge is scattered across a dozen different tools, or buried deep in obscure folders? You know, the kind of chaos that makes onboarding new members a nightmare and finding that crucial piece of information feel like a treasure hunt? Well, I just stumbled upon a GitHub project that's a total game-changer, and I couldn't wait to share it with you: Alexandrie.Imagine having a powerful, self-hosted knowledge base that's not just a simple note-taking app, but a full-fledged wiki designed for both individuals and teams. Alexandrie is an open-source platform that aims to be a robust alternative to tools like Notion or Confluence, giving you complete control over your data. The best part? You can get the entire full-stack application up and running with a single Docker command. Yes, you heard that right – one command to deploy your own knowledge empire!What truly makes Alexandrie shine is its Advanced Markdown Engine. This isn't your grandma's Markdown editor. We're talking native support for LaTeX for those complex mathematical expressions, integrated diagram building right within your notes (think flowcharts and structural diagrams without leaving your editor!), custom containers, interactive checkboxes, and even a snippet manager to save and reuse your frequently used code blocks or templates. Plus, it has speech-to-text, so you can dictate notes hands-free. This level of rich editing is a dream for technical documentation and collaborative project planning.For teams, Alexandrie offers Granular Organization and Access Control. It supports a multi-tenant architecture with Teams, Workspaces, Categories, and nested Documents. You can fine-tune user privileges with a 5-level access model (None, Read, Write, Admin, Owner) per node or workspace, ensuring sensitive information stays secure while fostering seamless collaboration. Sharing knowledge across your organization becomes simple and secure, with unique public links and robust group rules.Navigation and discovery are also top-notch. With the Command Center (Ctrl + K), you can navigate the app, execute actions, or trigger contextual operations instantly – a keyboard-driven dream for power users. Its full-text indexing means you can find anything quickly, with snippet highlights and precise relevancy scores. And for those of us who like to keep things organized, every workspace includes integrated Kanban boards for task management alongside your documentation. This means less context switching and more focus!Finally, the concept of Sovereign Assets & Storage Pipelines is incredibly appealing. Alexandrie ensures you maintain total ownership over your binaries, media streams, and backups. It relies on decoupled storage engines, including native S3 integration, to preserve performance without relying on external analytics or third-party dependencies. This means your data is truly yours, hosted where you want it.In a nutshell, Alexandrie is an incredibly exciting project that brings enterprise-grade knowledge management capabilities to the open-source world, all while being self-hostable and incredibly developer-friendly. If you're looking to consolidate your team's knowledge, improve documentation workflows, and take back control of your data, you absolutely need to check out Alexandrie on GitHub. It's a game-changer for productivity and organization!
key_takeaways: Alexandrie is a self-hosted, open-source knowledge base and wiki.
It features an advanced Markdown editor with integrated diagrams, LaTeX, and snippets.
Easy deployment via Docker and supports offline-first Progressive Web App (PWA) functionality.
Offers robust team collaboration with granular access control and multi-level organization.
Ensures data sovereignty with S3 integration and full control over your assets and backups.
readme_summary: Alexandrie is a self-hosted, open-source knowledge base and wiki platform that serves as an alternative to Notion, Confluence, and Obsidian. It offers advanced Markdown editing, offline-first capabilities via a PWA, team collaboration features, and enterprise-grade security like OIDC/SSO.
description: 📚 The open-source, offline-first Notion, Obsidian & Confluence alternative. Advanced Markdown, multi-tenant teams, OIDC/SSO, and local S3 backups. Deploy in one command.
